chunks: What was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Hamid, from Sayf ibn 'Umayrah, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from more than one of our companions, who said:
I said to Abī Ja'far عليه السلام: We are in a cold land where there is snow; should we perform sajdah upon the snow? He said: No. Rather, place something between yourself and it, cotton or linen.

key_terms.الثَّلْجُ: snow, the surface mentioned as unsuitable for direct sajdah here
key_terms.قُطْنًا: cotton, a material to be placed as a barrier
key_terms.كَتَّانًا: linen, a material to be placed as a barrier
key_terms.لَا: no, indicating prohibition or disallowance in this case
key_terms.نَسْجُدُ: we perform sajdah, referring to the act of prostration in salat

ai.seo_question: Can one perform sajdah directly on snow in cold lands?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sajdah in very cold conditions when snow is present. Imam Abī Ja'far عليه السلام instructs that one should not perform sajdah directly on snow, but should place a barrier such as cotton or linen between oneself and it.
